messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [CRITICAL] POP us-east1 (edge-mdw-03) seeing high packet loss to global CDN pool. Automated health checks failing 07:12 UTC. Error: 502/timeout spike. Paging @sre-oncall.

sre-alex: ack — on it. collecting scope. tagging @net-jen
sre-alex: quick check: are private customers affected or just hosted API traffic?
net-jen: seeing BGP flaps reported from ISP towards us-east1. initial MTR shows 40-60% loss at hop 5-6 (provider aggregation). digging.
eng-tim: noticed increase 5xx on /v1/generate and websocket disconnects. spike started ~07:11 UTC.
incident-bot: added incident-1234, created channel #inc-1234 (automated).
platform-ops: rolling traffic steering to us-east2 in 5m. will update weights to 0.8 -> us-east2, 0.2 -> us-east1.
sre-alex: do it. also enable emergency CDN origin failover for latency-sensitive routes.
net-jen: attaching traceroute and mtr from probe:
```
traceroute to edge-mdw-03 (34.213.55.8), 30 hops max
 1  10.20.0.1 0.8 ms
 2  54.239.22.1 1.2 ms
 3  100.64.12.5 3.8 ms
 4  * * *
 5  be-3.core.isp.net 150 ms 50% packet loss
 6  be-4.agg.isp.net 170 ms 60% packet loss
```
net-jen: indicates packet loss inside ISP aggregation/peering. looks like a provider-side regression.
cs-lee: CS alerted key customers with high SLA (Enterprise) — pushing note to their on-call. prepping a status update.
sre-alex: mitigation plan: 1) steer traffic away from us-east1 2) enable degraded responses for non-critical routes 3) throttle background batch jobs to reduce load 4) contact provider NOC and open ticket.
platform-ops: started traffic steer. CDN failover toggled for weights on latency routes. monitoring for error rate.
eng-tim: can we inject a 5xx fallback to prevent stuck streaming sessions? we have a config patch ready.
deploy-bot: deploy queued by eng-tim — started canary to 5% on us-east2.
net-jen: update: provider NOC confirms ongoing fiber maintenance, unexpected BGP behavior. they've opened ticket TKT-9876 and rolling back recent config.
sre-alex: numbers: pre-mitigation ~12% of global requests routed via edge-mdw-03 saw >200ms and 5xx rate jumped to 6%. after steering so far error rate dropped to 1.8% for routed traffic.
platform-ops: adjusting cache TTLs to 30s to reduce origin load during reroute.
cs-lee: CS update posted to status.redwood.ai/incidents/1234: initial, mitigation in progress, potential customer impact — sent to enterprise POCs.
net-jen: provider rollback in progress, but ETA unknown — monitoring BGP table for stability.
eng-tim: customers with Dedicated capacity: failover to dedicated pools in us-east2 initiated for accounts matching commit tags.
sre-alex: action items for night shift: keep traffic steering until provider confirms stable for 30m, watch for re-introduction of edge-mdw-03, escalate to cloud-bgp team if BGP flaps reappear. handing off to @sre-maya.
sre-maya: taking over. summary noted. will maintain watch and coordinate with net-jen and platform-ops. please post any outstanding creds or runbooks.
sre-alex: runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/edge-pop-failover (shared)
platform-ops: current status: us-east1 traffic weight now 0.12, error rate 1.2% overall. keeping reduced background jobs.
net-jen: provider reports partial stabilization; packet loss down to 15% at worst hop. still see intermittent flaps.
cs-lee: sent follow-up to enterprise POCs: "mitigation in progress, partial service degradation for <15% requests, next update in 30m" :email: 
sre-maya: will monitor until stable for 30m, then start gradual traffic return. if we see >2% 5xx on global, revert.
sre-maya: handing note to next oncall at 02:00 UTC — @sre-omar will take final watch.
sre-omar: ack. will monitor charts and keep incident open until provider confirms fully resolved.
incident-bot: incident-1234 status: mitigated -> monitoring. created timeline artifact.

sre-omar: final update at 08:46 UTC — provider confirmed rollback completed at 08:35 UTC, BGP stable, packet loss normalized. restoring traffic weights to normal over 10min. closing incident in 30m if metrics remain stable.
cs-lee: status update posted: root cause likely provider peering config change, mitigation: traffic steering, CDN failover, customer impact: ~12% requests experienced degraded latency/5xx, no data loss. customers notified.
incident-bot: incident-1234 CLOSED at 09:10 UTC — postmortem scheduled.
